newsitem.title: EGYPT: Tourism in Egypt breaks record highs.
newsitem.headline: Tourism in Egypt breaks record highs.

text.p: Egypt received a record 3.9 million tourists in 1996 and earned a record of more than $3 billion from the industry in the financial year 1995/96, an official at the tourism ministry said on Sunday.
"A total of 3,895,942 tourists visited Egypt in 1996, 24.3 percent more than the figure for 1995," the director general of the ministry's technical office, Sayyed Mehrez, told Reuters.
Tourists spent $3,009.1 million over 23.76 million nights in the financial year, which ended on June 30, Mehrez added.
Their expenditure was $2.3 million during 20.45 million nights in the previous financial year, he said.
The government said in a statement to parliament last month that it aimed to increase the number of tourists to 4.2 million in the financial year 1997/98.
Tourism in the 1995 calendar year had already matched the record-breaking year 1992. Attacks on tourist targets by Islamist militants had led to a slump in 1993 and 1994.

The last attack was in March last year, when gunmen massacred 18 Greek tourists outside a Cairo hotel. But it appeared to be an isolated incident and its effect on tourist arrivals was both minor and short-lived.
Tourism is Egypt's third largest source of foreign exchange, after remittances from Egyptians abroad and visible exports.
